name: Continuous molten-metal float glass
summary: Pilkington's float process makes flat glass by floating a continuous ribbon of molten glass on molten tin, giving smooth sheets without grinding and polishing.
description: Continuous flat-glass production flows molten glass over a liquid-metal bath, draws the ribbon off and anneals it. Pilkington’s later industrial implementation used molten tin; earlier metal-bath patents and an unsuccessful trial predated it.
tier_reason: A major reusable result, process or system within its field; broader multi-field or multi-generation dependence on this exact referent is not established.

impact.note: Cheaper, flatter glass that replaced older processes worldwide without changing what glass did, with few successors; scores imply tier 2, below the reviewed tier 1.

why: Plate glass needed costly grinding and polishing to be flat and clear, so a process giving smooth, flat glass directly promised large savings.

market.note: The configuration can be supplied or used in economic production, independently of the date and scope of any first offer.
